story: Five National Science Foundation projects, funded across six awards to University of Alaska campuses, put 18,647,929 obligated dollars of artificial intelligence to work reading five physical Alaska surfaces, with every performance clock starting August 1st or September 1st, 2026

claims.claim: NSF award 2630206 is titled I-Corps Translation Potential of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Satellite-Derived Nearshore Bathymetry and River Profiles.
claims.verbatim: I-Corps: Translation Potential of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Satellite-Derived Nearshore Bathymetry and River Profiles
claims.notes: The full title begins with I-Corps Translation Potential of. The shorter string is not the whole title. Colons appear in the source string only and never in deck prose.

claims.claim: NSF obligated 50,000 dollars to award 2630206 in fiscal year 2026.
claims.notes: estimatedTotalAmt and fundsObligatedAmt agree at 50000 for this award.

claims.claim: NSF dated award 2630206 August 19, 2026.
claims.notes: initAmendmentDate and latestAmendmentDate are both 08/19/2026, so this is a first and only action. It is the newest of the six awards.

claims.claim: Award 2630206 has a performance period running September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027.
claims.notes: expDate on the same record is 08/31/2027. One year exactly, the shortest horizon of the six.

claims.claim: Erin Trochim of the University of Alaska Fairbanks is the principal investigator on award 2630206.
claims.verbatim: Erin D Trochim
claims.notes: awardeeName is University of Alaska Fairbanks Campus. The record lists no coPDPI, so this is a single investigator award.

claims.claim: The abstract for award 2630206 says the project develops explainable artificial intelligence that converts satellite imagery into high resolution maps of underwater depth for coastlines, rivers and lakes.
claims.verbatim: This I-Corps project is based on the development of explainable artificial intelligence (AI) that converts satellite imagery into high-resolution maps of underwater depth (bathymetry) for coastlines, rivers, and lakes.
claims.notes: Verbatim first sentence of the abstract. THE SURFACE THIS PROJECT READS IS THE WATER.

claims.claim: The abstract for award 2630206 says the framework combines physics informed neural networks with interpretable architectures.
claims.verbatim: The framework combines physics-informed neural networks embedding radiative-transfer attenuation constraints with interpretable architectures.
claims.notes: Evidence this is a real model and not a label.

claims.claim: NSF filed award 2630206 under the program element ARTIFICIAL INTELL and COGNIT SCI.
claims.verbatim: ARTIFICIAL INTELL & COGNIT SCI, EXP PROG TO STIM COMP RES
claims.notes: NSF's own classification, not a reading of the abstract. The ampersand is in the source string only.

claims.claim: NSF obligated 3,824,575 dollars to the University of Alaska Anchorage under award 2614749.
claims.notes: awardeeName is University of Alaska Anchorage Campus. estimatedTotalAmt equals fundsObligatedAmt.

claims.claim: NSF obligated 913,037 dollars to the University of Alaska Fairbanks under award 2614751.
claims.notes: awardeeName is University of Alaska Fairbanks Campus. estimatedTotalAmt equals fundsObligatedAmt.

claims.claim: Awards 2614749 and 2614751 carry the identical project title, Collaborative Research FEC Transformative Bioprocessing and AI-Driven Frameworks for Sustainable Critical Mineral Recovery.
claims.verbatim: Collaborative Research: FEC: Transformative Bioprocessing and AI-Driven Frameworks for Sustainable Critical Mineral Recovery
claims.notes: The same title and a byte identical abstract appear on the separately fetched 2614749 record. This is why the deck counts five projects across six awards. Colons are in the source title only.

claims.claim: The two critical mineral awards together obligate 4,737,612 dollars.
claims.notes: Addition of two published figures, 3,824,575 plus 913,037. The sum is not printed on any NSF page and is presented as an addition, never as a figure NSF published.

claims.claim: Anchorage holds the larger of the two critical mineral awards, taking about four times what Fairbanks takes.
claims.verbatim: UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA ANCHORAGE
claims.notes: The ratio is 4.19 to 1, so about four times is safe and four times is not.

claims.claim: The critical mineral abstract says the initiative is led by the University of Alaska Anchorage in partnership with the University of Alaska Fairbanks, Montana Technological University and the University of Wyoming.
claims.verbatim: a use-inspired research initiative led by the University of Alaska Anchorage, in partnership with the University of Alaska Fairbanks, Montana Technological University, and the University of Wyoming
claims.notes: NSF's own abstract says Anchorage leads, which independently corroborates C13.

claims.claim: NSF dated both critical mineral awards August 5, 2026.
claims.notes: The 2614751 record carries the same date value.

claims.claim: Both critical mineral awards run September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2030.
claims.notes: expDate on both records is 08/31/2030.

claims.claim: Brandon Briggs is the principal investigator on the Anchorage critical mineral award.
claims.verbatim: Brandon R Briggs
claims.notes: Four co-PIs are listed, three at alaska.edu and one at uwyo.edu.

claims.claim: Srijan Aggarwal is the principal investigator on the Fairbanks critical mineral award.
claims.verbatim: Srijan Aggarwal
claims.notes: The 2614751 record lists no coPDPI field.

claims.claim: The critical mineral abstract says the project applies reinforcement learning controllers within a bioprocess digital twin integrated with microgrid simulators.
claims.value: reinforcement-learning controllers in a bioprocess digital twin
claims.verbatim: applies reinforcement-learning controllers within a bioprocess digital twin integrated with microgrid simulators
claims.notes: The identical string appears in the 2614751 abstract. THE SURFACE THIS PROJECT READS IS THE WASTE, coal refuse and ash. The organism named is Shewanella oneidensis.

claims.claim: NSF award 2608510 is titled Collaborative Research Frameworks Geophysical AI-driven Integration and Assimilation GAIA.
claims.verbatim: Collaborative Research: Frameworks: Geophysical AI-driven Integration & Assimilation (GAIA)
claims.notes: The source title uses an ampersand. Colons and the ampersand are in the source string only.

claims.claim: NSF obligated 1,772,170 dollars to the University of Alaska Fairbanks for GAIA.
claims.notes: This is the UAF share of a collaborative award and is not the whole project's national budget.

claims.claim: NSF dated the GAIA award July 10, 2026 and it runs August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2032.
claims.notes: date is 07/10/2026 and expDate is 07/31/2032 on the same record.

claims.claim: Carl Tape is the principal investigator on GAIA.
claims.verbatim: Carl H Tape

claims.claim: GAIA lists three co-principal investigators, Michael West, Franz Meyer and Ronni Grapenthin, all at alaska.edu addresses.
claims.verbatim: Michael E West mewest@alaska.edu
claims.notes: The other two coPDPI entries are Franz J Meyer fjmeyer@alaska.edu and Ronni Grapenthin rgrapenthin@alaska.edu.

claims.claim: The GAIA abstract says the team trains fast surrogate models coupled to incoming observations to produce real time digital twins that forecast geohazards.
claims.verbatim: the team trains fast surrogate models that approximate expensive physics simulations and couples them to incoming observations through data assimilation to produce real-time digital twins that forecast geohazards
claims.notes: The named hazards elsewhere in the abstract are earthquakes, landslides and floods.

claims.claim: The GAIA abstract says the investigators test the full system on landslides in Alaska and the Pacific Northwest.
claims.verbatim: The investigators test the full system on landslides in Alaska and the Pacific Northwest.
claims.notes: THE SURFACE THIS PROJECT READS IS THE MOVING GROUND. This is what makes GAIA an Alaska ground story rather than generic cyberinfrastructure.

claims.claim: NSF award 2532372 is titled NSF Critical Mineral Accelerator Engine in Alaska and is held by the University of Alaska Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: NSF Critical Mineral Accelerator Engine in Alaska
claims.notes: awardeeName is University of Alaska Fairbanks Campus.

claims.claim: The Engine award carries an estimated total amount of 15,000,000 dollars.
claims.notes: HARD CONSTRAINT. This is estimatedTotalAmt on a ten year cooperative agreement, not money in hand. Any deck line must read as estimated or expected total, NEVER as awarded or obligated. See C29.

claims.claim: NSF has obligated 10,500,000 dollars of the Engine award in fiscal year 2026.
claims.notes: 4,500,000 dollars below the estimated total. The obligated figure is the only one that belongs in a money total.

claims.claim: The Engine award runs August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2036, a ten year period.
claims.notes: startDate is 08/01/2026 on the same record. The longest horizon of the six awards.

claims.claim: The Engine is a cooperative agreement rather than a standard grant.
claims.verbatim: Cooperative Agreement
claims.notes: The other five awards are all transType Standard Grant. This is why the Engine's total is staged rather than obligated at once, and it supports C28.

claims.claim: Lee Munk is the principal investigator on the Engine award.
claims.verbatim: Lee A Munk

claims.claim: The Engine abstract says the project intends to integrate geological, geochemical, geophysical, remote sensing and legacy data into AI based systems to identify concealed mineral deposits.
claims.verbatim: integrating geological, geochemical, geophysical, remote-sensing, and legacy data into AI-based systems, including metal-isotope geochemical approaches to identify concealed mineral deposits
claims.notes: THE SURFACE THIS PROJECT READS IS THE CONCEALED ROCK, ore bodies nobody has found.

claims.claim: The Engine abstract says methods will combine data integration, machine learning and uncertainty analysis with laboratory experiments and field validation.
claims.verbatim: Methods will combine data integration, machine learning, and uncertainty analysis with laboratory experiments and field validation, directly linking discovery to recovery and production decisions.

claims.claim: A co-principal investigator on the Engine award is listed at a nana.com email address.
claims.verbatim: lance D miller lance.miller@nana.com
claims.notes: HARD CONSTRAINT. Write this as a co-PI listed at a NANA email address, NEVER as NANA Regional Corporation holding a formal role, because the API record does not name an employer. The lowercase lance is in the source. The coPDPI list also carries Erin.Whitney@hq.doe.gov, ssmasterman@alaska.edu and Liz@endolithmining.com.

claims.claim: The Engine abstract says coordinated partnerships among academia, Alaska Native Corporations, industry, tech start ups, national laboratories, state and federal agencies and nonprofits will align research with operational needs.
claims.value: Alaska Native Corporations named in the abstract
claims.verbatim: among academia, Alaska Native Corporations, industry, tech start-ups, national laboratories, state and federal agencies, and nonprofit organizations will align research with operational needs
claims.notes: Independent corroboration for C35.

claims.claim: The six awards obligate 18,647,929 dollars in total.
claims.notes: HARD CONSTRAINT. Arithmetic across six primary records. 50,000 plus 3,824,575 plus 913,037 plus 1,588,147 plus 1,772,170 plus 10,500,000 equals 18,647,929. This is OBLIGATED dollars and is NOT total project value, which would be 23,147,929 if the Engine's estimate were substituted. It is also only the University of Alaska share of three collaborative projects whose national budgets are larger. Say obligated, and say about 18.6 million.

claims.claim: Every one of the six awards has a performance start date of either August 1, 2026 or September 1, 2026.
claims.value: 6 of 6 clocks start August 1st or September 1st
claims.notes: HARD CONSTRAINT ON INTERPRETATION. 2608510 and 2532372 start 08/01/2026. 2630206, 2614749, 2614751 and 2536745 start 09/01/2026. These are ordinary federal fiscal and academic start dates, so the deck presents the alignment as a fact and NEVER as evidence of coordination.

claims.claim: The five projects expire on four different dates spanning August 31, 2027 to July 31, 2036.
claims.notes: Bathymetry 08/31/2027, critical minerals 08/31/2030 on both awards, fire weather 08/31/2030, GAIA 07/31/2032, Engine 07/31/2036. Four distinct expiry dates across five projects, because two projects share 08/31/2030.

claims.claim: An NSF award API query for Alaska awardees with award dates from August 16, 2026 to August 26, 2026 returns exactly two records.
claims.verbatim: "rpp":50,"totalCount":2
claims.notes: rpp was 50 and totalCount was 2, so the result is not truncated. HARD CONSTRAINT ON SCOPE. The query filters on awardee state, so an award for Alaska work held by an out of state institution would not appear. Phrase as awards to Alaska awardees.

claims.claim: One of the two Alaska awards in that ten day window is the AI bathymetry award and the other is a mathematical biology award on phylogenetic networks.
claims.verbatim: Collaborative Research: Fast and sound coalescent-based inference of semi-directed phylogenetic networks from genome-scale data
claims.notes: The second award is 2554614, PI Elizabeth Allman at UAF, dated 08/20/2026, fundProgramName MATHEMATICAL BIOLOGY.

claims.claim: The other Alaska award in that window obligates 289,888 dollars to the University of Alaska Fairbanks.

The abstract for NSF award 2536745 says the research team will use statistical and machine learning techniques to characterize the geographic and seasonal patterns of hazardous fire weather across Alaska.
claims.verbatim: Using historical weather reanalysis data and statistical and machine-learning techniques, the research team will characterize the geographic and seasonal patterns of hazardous fire weather and identify windows of conditions favorable for safe prescribed burning across Alaska and the broader Northern Pacific Boreal-Arctic region.
claims.notes: THE SURFACE THIS PROJECT READS IS THE BURNING WEATHER. The abstract writes machine-learning hyphenated, which is how a literal search for the two-word form misses it.

claims.claim: NSF classifies the Alaska fire weather toolkit award under the program Artificial Intelligence (AI).
claims.verbatim: Artificial Intelligence (AI), FIRE-Wildland Fire, INTERDISCIPLINARY PROPOSALS, Improv Undergrad STEM Ed(IUSE), EXP PROG TO STIM COMP RES, UNDERGRADUATE EDUCATION
claims.notes: The record carries progRefCode 075Z, the same AI reference code carried by 2614749, 2614751 and 2608510. The bathymetry award 2630206 carries 6856 under ARTIFICIAL INTELL and COGNIT SCI instead.

claims.claim: NSF obligated 1,588,147 dollars to the University of Alaska Fairbanks for the fire weather toolkit award, which runs September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2030.
claims.notes: PI is Christine Waigl, award date 07/31/2026. Title is Collaborative Research FIRE-WUI A research-informed fire weather toolkit to advance controlled burning in Alaska.

claims.claim: The UAF news index for August 9, 2026 to August 21, 2026 carries fifteen headlines and none of them names any of these six awards. The fifteen, newest first, are: Veteran journalist and author joins UAF as Snedden chair, 2026-08-21; Alaska Defense Forum 2026 focuses on community-military ties, 2026-08-21; Uncorking the secrets of a tiny bottle of volcanic ash, 2026-08-21; Shapes of Western Alaska bays influence local flood danger, 2026-08-20; Expanded UAF, military partnership looks north, 2026-08-19; Faudree, Sikes, Shallcross named 2026 Usibelli Award winners, 2026-08-13; Time capsule: Looking for a few good wood frogs, 2026-08-13; Accelerated rates of warming in the Arctic continue, 2026-08-12; 100,000 dollar planetarium gift celebrates alumni association centennial, 2026-08-12; Festival will satisfy currant curiosity, 2026-08-12; UAF leads AI project to strengthen Alaska's rural power grids, 2026-08-11; How do Alaska animals sleep in the summer?, 2026-08-11; New instrument will aid environmental science and industry, 2026-08-10; Tickets available for UAF Business Leader of the Year event, 2026-08-10; Week's events: Robert Hannon, sleep, Alaska Native language archive, string band, 2026-08-09.
claims.verbatim: Expanded UAF, military partnership looks north
claims.notes: HARD CONSTRAINT. Fifteen headlines dated August 9th to August 21st were listed on the index as fetched, and none names the Engine, GAIA, bathymetry, fire weather, rare earth elements or critical minerals. This is a claim about ONE index page on ONE day and is NOT a claim that nobody reported these awards. The index paginates. The verbatim is one listed headline, offered as proof the page loaded. ENUMERATION ADDED 2026-08-26 DURING THE ART BUILD. Slide 08 draws one square per headline at its true date on a declared measured axis, so the fifteen dates became load-bearing and had to be in the record rather than in the showrunner's head. The showrunner re-fetched the same primary URL, got exactly fifteen headlines across August 9th to August 21st, and the August 11th AI headline came back matching C47's verbatim character for character, which re-confirms both claims. The count and the conclusion are unchanged; only the supporting detail is now written down.

claims.claim: The same UAF news index carries a separate artificial intelligence headline dated August 11, 2026 about rural power grids.
claims.verbatim: UAF leads AI project to strengthen Alaska's rural power grids
claims.notes: A check on the story's framing. UAF does publicise AI work, so the absence of these six awards from its own index is specific to these awards rather than a blanket silence about AI. This is a DIFFERENT project (AURORA-AI, covered by this page on 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-12) and must never be counted among the six.

claims.claim: Alaska's 2026 wildfire season formally ends August 31st, the day before the fire weather award's performance period begins.
claims.verbatim: Alaska's fire season formally ends August 31st
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: SCOUT-SOURCED AND NOT RE-FETCHED BY THE FACT-CHECKER. Use only if a later phase re-verifies it against the page. The juxtaposition with C45's September 1st start is true arithmetic on two dates but the season-end date itself needs a fetch before any slide prints it.

killed.claim: A fifth award, 2536745, was examined and excluded because no AI or machine learning language appears anywhere in its abstract.
killed.why: FALSE on the primary document, and this was the showrunner's own error, caught by the fact-checker. The abstract contains machine-learning hyphenated (C43) and NSF files the award under its Artificial Intelligence (AI) program with AI reference code 075Z (C44). The showrunner's regex searched for the two-word form and missed the hyphen. The award is FOLDED BACK IN, which moves the deck from four projects and 17,059,782 dollars to five projects and 18,647,929 dollars. No slide, caption or comment may state that an award was examined and excluded.

killed.claim: No Alaska newsroom has reported any of these awards.
killed.why: Unprovable universal negative. The DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint returned a CAPTCHA rather than results, so no search was executed. The scouts' front page reads are not reproducible evidence. Replaced by C46, a narrow claim about one index page, and tempered by C47.

killed.claim: Award 2630206 is titled Explainable Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Satellite-Derived Nearshore Bathymetry and River Profiles.
killed.why: Truncated. The full title begins I-Corps Translation Potential of. Quoting the short form as the title misquotes a primary document. Corrected at C01.

killed.claim: The Engine award is a 15 million dollar award to UAF.
killed.why: Misleading. 15,000,000 is estimatedTotalAmt on a ten year cooperative agreement and only 10,500,000 is obligated. See C28, C29 and C31.

killed.claim: NANA Regional Corporation is a partner on the Engine award.
killed.why: Overreaches the record. The API lists a co-PI at lance.miller@nana.com but names no employer or organisational role. Kept only in the softened form at C35, corroborated by C36.

killed.claim: The critical mineral project is a 4.7 million dollar Anchorage project.
killed.why: Incomplete. 4,737,612 is the sum of the two University of Alaska awards only. Montana Technological University and the University of Wyoming are named partners whose awards were not fetched and are not in the total.

killed.claim: The alignment of every start date on August 1st or September 1st shows the awards were coordinated.
killed.why: The dates are verified at C38 but the inference is not. Federal fiscal and academic calendars produce these dates routinely. No source supports coordination.

killed.claim: These awards represent roughly 18.6 million dollars of AI research funding for Alaska.
killed.why: Survives only in the hedged form at C37. As written it invites two errors, treating obligated dollars as project value and treating the University of Alaska share of three collaborative projects as the whole.
